top_findings.title: standings() returns a wrong table for "Série A" queries — normalize() collapses the division letter so Serie A/B/C merge
top_findings.evidence: normalize() (src/lib.rs:412-453) drops tokens of len<=2, so "serie-a"/"Serie A"/"Série A" all fold to "serie"; contains() (src/lib.rs:454-456) then matches BR-Football-Dataset.csv rows whose tournament is Serie A, Serie B AND Serie C (distinct tournament values confirmed: Serie A/B/C). The factual probe calls standings with competition="serie-a" first (factual_accuracy.py:303) and gets a bloated 2019 table: _factual.json reports 5 Atlético/Athletico rows (expected 2) — BR-Football spells Paranaense as both "Atletico Paranaense" and "Athletico Paranaense" (unreconciled) and adds Atletico Goianiense/Acreano/Alagoinhas from the lower tiers. factual_accuracy=0.0 in scores.json.
top_findings.suggestion: Do not fold the division letter: normalize competition separately (keep the A/B/C suffix), or match tournament exactly rather than via substring; and reconcile the Atletico/Athletico spelling variants before building the table. The canonical "Brasileirão" path (Brasileirao_Matches.csv) is already correct — route Série A queries to it.
